content: I’ll trace how depfile-discovered edges and dyndep-added outputs are connected during scanning, then add a focused regression test and make the smallest scheduling fix that preserves normal dirty-state behavior.

The supported failure mode is an ordering mutation during one dirty scan: the depfile input is visited as a leaf before the order-only path loads dyndep and gives that same node a producer. I need the remainder of `RecomputeNodeDirty` and its state-reset helpers to choose whether the safe fix is a local second-pass check or invalidating/revisiting affected dependents.

The minimal safe fix is a post-traversal state check of all inputs. It catches both dirtiness and readiness changes caused when a later input loads dyndep and retroactively gives an earlier depfile input a producer. I’ll add the reverse-order regression case alongside the existing depfile/dyndep connection test.

The implementation and regression test are in place. I’ll now run the focused test first, then the full test binary if the focused check passes; any compile or semantic failure will be treated as evidence to refine the patch.
